_what: Re-adjudication of the 11 check_creepage findings against the CORRECT IPC-2221 Table 6-1 row for each item pair. check_creepage.py hardcodes only B2 (external UNCOATED) and B1 (internal) and has no way to declare a coated board, so it over-reports every outer-layer pair on any soldermasked design.

_rows_verified.note: All three tabulations agree on every cell used here. 51-100 V: B1 0.10, B2 0.60, B3 1.50, B4 0.13, A5 0.13, A6 0.50, A7 0.13 mm. 101-150 V: B1 0.20, B2 0.60, B4 0.40, A6 0.80 mm.
_rows_verified.correction_to_the_brief: The instruction said exposed copper stays on B2 (0.60 mm). Per IPC-2221 section 6.3.4, quoted verbatim by the Altair source, that is not what the standard says: 'The assembly electrical clearances of lands and leads that are not conformably coated require the electrical clearance requirements stated in category A6.' B2/B3 are for uncoated CONDUCTORS on a bare board with no coating at all. Where a board IS polymer-coated but its LANDS are exposed by mask openings, the standard directs those lands to A6 = 0.50 mm at 51-100 V (0.80 mm at 101-150 V), not to B2's 0.60 mm. Adjudicated on that basis, which is very slightly more permissive for the 51-100 V pads and STRICTER for the one 114 V pair.

_basis_and_its_caveat.board: soldermask on both outer layers (LPI), no conformal coating on the assembly
_basis_and_its_caveat.row_applied_to_masked_trace_or_tented_vi: B4 (external conductors with permanent polymer coating, any elevation)
_basis_and_its_caveat.judgement_call_disclosed: Whether LPI soldermask qualifies as IPC's 'permanent polymer coating' is a genuine interpretation, widely accepted in industry but not free of doubt: a conservative reading points at mask registration tolerance and coverage thinning over via barrels and at trace shoulders. Every number below is stated so the owner can re-adjudicate on B2 if they prefer the conservative reading - the affected count is given.
_basis_and_its_caveat.supporting_fact: IPC 6.3.4 excludes this configuration from 'any application requiring protection from harsh, humid, contaminated environments'. Per H1-Q5 the enclosure is SEALED and non-metallic, which is the favourable case for that exclusion, not the adverse one.

items.why_unfixable: HTSSOP-20, 0.65 mm lead pitch. 0.375 mm is the gap between two of the part's own adjacent pins. No board layout can change a vendor lead frame.

items.note: This is the item that generated 217 pairs under 0.600 mm, the worst at 0.2031 mm. ALL 217 are trace-to-trace under soldermask, and the minimum of the whole population, 0.2031 mm, clears B4's 0.13 mm by 56 percent. Two fixer attempts and one retracted edit were spent on a requirement that does not apply to this geometry. Under a conservative B2 reading it fails and the 217-pair count stands.

items.why_unfixable: The track is U22's own pin-7 escape inside its courtyard; the clearance is set by the 0.65 mm lead pitch it has to leave from.
Two of U20's own adjacent pins.

TPS2378-class PD controller in SOIC-8. 0.200 mm is the inter-lead gap of a 1.27 mm-pitch SOIC, i.e. the package as TI ships it. TI qualifies the part for 100 V operation with VDD and VSS on adjacent pins, so the governing spec here is the PACKAGE's own pin-to-pin rating, not IPC-2221's board-spacing table. Recorded at P6 as the reason the .kicad_dru HV rules carry a pad-pair exclusion.

items.verdict: STILL FAILS by 0.600 mm - and the correct row is STRICTER than the reported one
items.why_unfixable: Same SOIC-8 lead frame. This is the full 114 V across the rectified rail sitting between pin 1 and pin 9 of one package. Worth stating plainly in the design document because it is the single largest nominal shortfall on the board, and it is entirely a package-selection consequence: it would only be fixable by choosing a PD controller in a wider-pitch or creepage-optimised package.

summary.remaining_all_one_class: package-internal: every one is a pad of a single footprint against another pad or against that same footprint's own escape, inside U1 (7), U22 (2) or U20 (1)
summary.if_owner_prefers_conservative_B2_reading: item 2 returns as a 217-pair shortfall with a 0.2031 mm worst case; the other 10 are unchanged either way because they fail every applicable row

_STATUS_NOT_ADOPTED.verdict: NOT ADOPTED. This adjudication is a technical analysis only; it does NOT resolve item 2 and must not be quoted as having done so.
_STATUS_NOT_ADOPTED.why: The fresh-context verify-reviewer found that connector-icd.md rev A6 s5.1 states verbatim: "The 0.13 mm permanent polymer coating column (B4) is NOT claimed. Standard LPI soldermask is not a qualified conformal coating." The .kicad_dru header says the same. ICD-01 is FROZEN and three boards inherit it, and the very same section derives the 0.635 mm board-wide figure that s5.4 imposes on every daughter s 48 V copper - a derivation that exists BECAUSE B4 was refused. A work/ JSON cannot reverse a frozen ICD. Adopting B4 requires an ICD rev A7 with the owner s signature and a re-derivation of the daughter inheritance.
_STATUS_NOT_ADOPTED.consequence_until_then: The 217-pair shortfall at 0.2031 mm against 0.600 mm STANDS as an open owner item.
_STATUS_NOT_ADOPTED.aggravating_fact_found_by_the_reviewer: The far side of that gap is not a passive indicator. /poe/LED_Y_A has exactly two pads - J1 pin 17 and R7 pin 2 - and R7 is a 330 R 0603 whose pin 1 is on +3V3. So the failure product of the 0.2031 mm gap is 57 V injected onto +3V3 through 330 R, unclamped, and +3V3 leaves the board on J3 pins 12 and 14 to every daughter board. No PESD device sits on any LED net (D31/D32/D40/D41/D42 are all on expansion signals; D10 TPD4E1U06 clamps only the MDI). This raises the consequence well above a cosmetic spacing miss.
_STATUS_NOT_ADOPTED.recommendation: Mitigate physically regardless of which IPC row wins - reroute LED_Y_A out of the tap pocket, or clamp +3V3 - because the highest-consequence gap on the board is currently defended only by soldermask. That also makes the B4 question moot for this pair.
_STATUS_NOT_ADOPTED.what_survives: The row table itself is verified and correct, and items 1 and 3-11 are unaffected: all ten fail every applicable row and remain package-internal waivers. The IPC 6.3.4 finding that exposed lands go to A6 (0.50 / 0.80 mm) rather than back to B2 also stands on its own.
